Subject: Planned patch window for Private cluster (request)

Hi Chloe and Redwood team,

We want to schedule the July maintenance so we can accept the new runtime micropatch (security + perf). Targeting Thursday 2025-08-07 00:00-04:00 UTC. Key asks:
- Minimal disruption for production traffic (FinTrust uses private VPC, 4 availability subnets)
- Clear rollback path if model-serving latency regresses
- Confirmation on whether KV cache eviction will require coordinated client restarts

Can you propose a pinning/evacuation approach? We prefer a blue-green style cut with short-lived pin waves, but open to alternatives if you recommend. Atlantic Cloud netops (cc) needs any BGP prep details as early as Friday.

Thanks,
Ravi Kumar
Operations Lead — FinTrust

Hi Ravi — thanks for the heads up.

High-level proposal (quick bullets):
1) Blue-green pin waves by subnet: pin group A (subnets 1+2) then group B (3+4). Each wave: 20% canary traffic -> 60% ramp -> full cut.
2) LB rehome step before pin: re-point 10% of L7 load to canary pool to validate routing and TCP keepalives.
3) KV cache strategy: perform prefix-preserving KV shadow writes during canary; only evict on full cut. No client restarts expected if TTLs respected, but we need a quick client toggle for cache-bypass (we'll provide a header).
4) Rollback ladder: automated revert (model pin revert + KV cache backfill) + network drain reversal. Rollback trigger is any 5-minute p99 > 350ms or error spike > 2x baseline.

I'll loop in Karthik and Marcus to give technical steps and the exact command sequences (and scripts). Can Atlantic Cloud provide a prep window for BGP prep/config freeze? We want changes committed by Friday EOD to allow a dry run Monday.

Cheers,
Chloe Martin
Senior PM, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Adding the low-level runbook and gating logic here. Summary of steps (for ops playbook):

Pre-window (T-72h):
- Share final pin matrix (attached) and confirm allowed maintenance IP ranges with Atlantic Cloud.
- Snapshot leader KV shards and export metadata; create read-only snapshot for backfill.
- Start a dark-write (shadow) path: new runtime writes to both old and new model backends for canary traffic.

T-1h (bridge):
- Place target subnets into passive mode (LB connection rehome to canary pool) using weighted DNS / L7 config.
- Warm model caches on canary nodes with synthetic seed traffic (5m soak).
- Enable fine-grained tracing and stats flush (1s resolution) to S3 for rapid STAMP-based rollup.

Cut wave (per-subnet, concurrent safety limits):
- Canary (20%, 10m): monitor p50/p90/p99, error rate, and token-cost delta.
- Ramp (to 60%, 15m): verify KV write shadow success >99.5% and no client-500s.
- Full (100%, 10m): finalize pin.

Rollback choreography: automated script rollback-scripts.sh will:
- Re-pin traffic to previous model version
- Re-ignite old model nodes and rehydrate KV snapshot
- Re-run LB weights to previous state and reverse BGP withdraws if applied
- Emit audit events to the control plane and notify on-call channel

Observability gating: if either p99 breaches threshold or token-cost delta > 12% for two consecutive windows, abort and rollback. The scripts are idempotent; we must run them from bastion with 2FA.

I'll attach the patched scripts and the pin matrix spreadsheet. Marcus will add the network drain steps.

—Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer

Network notes from Atlantic Cloud coordination (action items):
- BGP prep: we'll announce the canary next-hops using an isolated community tag; do not withdraw the production route until full cut confirmed. NetOps will pre-stage ACLs for the LB IPs.
- Drain plan: perform L4 graceful drain on canary nodes (conn timeout 120s), then L7 rehome if healthy. If rollback triggers, re-inject production routes and instruct LBs to fail back weights.
- Cross-subnet traffic shaping: rate-limit cache-fill at 200 rps for the first 10 minutes to avoid overheating shared storage.

Attached is the network-drain-play.pdf with a checklist for NetOps and a stub runbook for emergency rehoming.

Marcus Lin
